subject.title: fix(heartbeat): stop reporting success after tool failures

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `observeToolTerminal` as the shared host-owned contract for mutation failure and recovery semantics across all agent harnesses?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and proven, but this additive plugin-harness API and its failure-precedence behavior establish a durable ownership boundary that repository policy reserves for explicit owner review.

options.title: Approve the shared contract
options.body: Accept the host-owned observer as the canonical cross-harness terminal-outcome boundary and land after refreshing the branch and completing exact-head checks.

options.title: Narrow the initial scope
options.body: Restrict the change to the Codex heartbeat regression until maintainers define a smaller or internal-only cross-harness contract.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Keep the existing behavior until a designated owner is prepared to maintain the new terminal-outcome contract across every bundled harness.

recommendation.title: Approve the shared contract
recommendation.body: Accept the host-owned observer as the canonical cross-harness terminal-outcome boundary and land after refreshing the branch and completing exact-head checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most closely connects this person to both heartbeat execution and adjacent Codex runtime ownership, which are the two sides of the decision.
